_notes: ONE LADDER FOR EVERY FACTION (Kyle, 2026-10-27: 'keep the wow tiers of rep... there will be a lot').
The tiers below are the WoW-standard eight and they are defined ONCE, here, shared by every faction.
A faction block carries only who it is, where its reputation comes from, and what standing buys - never
its own ladder. That is what lets one UI tab list fifty factions without fifty different scales, and it
means adding a faction is a block of data and nothing else.
Thresholds are cumulative from Neutral, exactly as WoW: Friendly 3000, Honored 9000, Revered 21000,
Exalted 42000. Negative standing is defined too - nothing in the game drives rep down yet, but the
ladder has to support it before something does, or the first hostile faction rewrites this file.
THE NUMBERS DO TWO DIFFERENT JOBS. A zone's quests are worth enough together to carry a player into
Revered - that is the real path and the one that tells the story. Exalted is finished on kills, and
only kills from enemies the faction has an actual stake in. There is deliberately no flat 'dungeon
mobs give rep' rule: it would make the optimal play farming the easiest trash in the easiest room,
and killing a mushroom should not earn standing with a library.

crimson_codex.name: The Crimson Codex
crimson_codex.description: Blood elf arcanists who came down a fissure three years ago to index a cavern that did not exist, and have not finished.

leader.title: Codex-Master
leader.name: Ilarien Duskwaking
leader.line: Three years, eleven thousand entries, and one cavern that keeps producing things I have no column for.

crimson_codex._lore_note: Shown on the faction's detail panel. Written as the Codex would have it written - they are the ones keeping the record, and they are not neutral about themselves.
lore: A party of blood elves surveying the Ruins of Dalaran found a fissure in ground they had already mapped. It had not been there the month before. It went down further than their lamps, and kept going, and opened into a cavern the size of a county with a light hanging in the middle of it that nobody has reached since.

That was three years ago, in the same year the Integration rewrote the world and a great many things opened at once. The Codex do not describe the cavern as a discovery. They describe it as a find, which is a word for something that was already there, and they have been very careful to keep using it.

They came to catalogue, not to settle, and they will correct you on the distinction. Eleven thousand entries in three years: every crystal, every column, every fungal stand, each with a number and a provenance and a column it belongs in. Their stated purpose is to have the place properly written down before anyone else can claim it. Their actual conviction, which none of them will put in a report, is that a thing properly written down is a thing owned.

The index has begun to fail. Forty-one entries now have a number, a provenance, and no column that fits, and the count is rising. There is Dalaran masonry two hundred spans below Dalaran that nobody carried down. There is crystal growing to a tolerance no mineral holds. And under the Sporefall something has spent three years reading the Codex's own work through its contamination of their camp, and has started writing entries better than theirs.

They are precise, dry, faintly superior, and far more rattled than any of them will admit. They are also, and they know it, newcomers: they arrived the same year you did, in a place that is the same age as both of you, and not one person in Kael's Bastion has a prior claim on anything in it.

quest_rep._comment: Per quest, by shape. kill_boss objectives pay the boss rate; the named capstones pay more.

_comment: Only enemies the Codex has a stake in. Dissidents are ex-colleagues, Interlopers are rivals for
the same dig, Revenants sit on the prize, and the Deep Bloom is the thing reading them back.
The wildlife pays nothing, however deep the cave it lives in.
What standing actually buys. These are the GATES - they work, and they are not displayed on the
faction panel (Kyle, 2026-10-27: the panel is information only). Rewards will eventually span gear,
crafting recipes, recruits, quests and whole zones unlocked, so a reward ladder is not worth drawing
until it can show all of that honestly.
vendor_stock gates Quartermaster Sylvaine's shelves; quests gates the deeper Archive line and the
Exalted capstone; recruit is the one companion the Codex will release to somebody in their record.

orgrimmar.name: Orgrimmar
orgrimmar.description: The orc capital and the Horde's spine: the city Thrall built out of a landing site, and everything it has had to hold since.

leader.title: Warchief
leader.name: Thrall
leader.line: We were given nothing. We took a desert and called it home, and we will not apologise for the taking.

lore: The Horde came ashore in Durotar with nothing but what they carried and built a capital out of red stone and salvage. Orgrimmar is not a beautiful city and nobody in it pretends otherwise. It is a city that exists because the alternative was not existing.

Thrall runs it, and runs it carefully. He was raised in a human internment camp and freed his people out of one, and the experience left him with an instinct that sits oddly on a Warchief: he would rather hold what the Horde has than take more. Not everyone under him agrees, and the ones who do not are loud.

The city's standing with you is not sentiment. Orgrimmar keeps a count of who held the Barrens road, who cleared the Kolkar off the water, and who was there when the Burning Blade came up out of the Chasm under the city's own floor. The count is kept by quartermasters, not by poets.

Three years ago the world was rewritten and a great many people arrived who had never been born here. Orgrimmar took them in faster than anywhere else on the continent, and the Warchief has never explained why in public. Those close to him suspect it is because he knows exactly what it is to be somewhere you did not choose to be.

kill_rep._comment: The Horde's standing enemies in its own territory - the cult under the city, the centaur on the Barrens road, the quilboar in the fields, the harpies on the ridge.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. The system supports them; the content is not written.

darkspear_tribe.name: The Darkspear Tribe
darkspear_tribe.description: Jungle trolls who lost their islands twice and took them back once, and have been Horde ever since on terms they negotiated themselves.

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Kang'ari
leader.line: We been driven off dis water before. We came back. Dat is da whole of what you need to know about us.

lore: The Darkspear were a dying tribe on a sinking island when the Horde found them, and they have never once let anyone describe that as a rescue. It was a bargain. They have kept their end of it with a thoroughness that embarrasses larger peoples.

Then Zalazane took the isles with hexes and turned their own people into something that walks at them out of the surf, and the tribe moved to the mainland and started again. The ones who stayed are still out there on the water, and the tribe does not call them lost. They call them not back yet.

The trolls run their own trainers, their own spiritwalkers and their own count of favours owed, separate from Orgrimmar's and older. Standing with the Darkspear is not standing with the Horde. It is standing with people who remember who came out on the water with them and who did not.
They are warm, funny and entirely unsentimental about death, which outsiders consistently misread as either of the first two things.

kill_rep._comment: Zalazane's hexed and the naga on the reefs - the two things keeping the tribe off its own islands.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. The system supports them; the content is not written.

the_forsaken.name: The Forsaken
the_forsaken.description: The dead who woke up with their minds intact, took Lordaeron's capital back from the Scourge, and have been explaining themselves to nobody since.

leader.title: Banshee Queen
leader.name: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner
leader.line: We were not given our freedom. I took it, and I will not be asked to be grateful for a thing I had to tear loose.

lore: The Scourge raised Lordaeron's dead and bound them, and then the binding slipped. What stood up afterwards remembered everything: their names, their houses, their families, and exactly what had been done to them and by whom. The Forsaken are what that leaves behind.

They took the capital's undercroft, walled it, and made a nation out of a sewer under a throne room that still has their old king's bloodstain on the floor. They do not describe this as tragic. They describe it as theirs.

The Apothecarium is the heart of it and the part that worries everyone, allies included. The Forsaken are the only people on the continent researching the plague that made them, and their stated reason - a cure - is not one that survives much scrutiny from the people who have read the ledgers.

What they will not forgive is the Scarlet Crusade, who kill the Forsaken on sight for being what the Scourge made them, and the cults still working for the thing that made them in the first place. Standing with the Forsaken is largely a tally of which of those two you have reduced.
They are dry, tired, blackly funny, and extremely difficult to impress. They have been dead for years. Very little is new.

kill_rep._comment: The Scarlet Crusade, who kill them on sight, and the cults still serving the thing that made them.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. The system supports them; the content is not written.

steamwheedle_cartel.name: The Steamwheedle Cartel
steamwheedle_cartel.description: Goblin traders who will sell to anyone, protect no one, and keep a port open through wars that close everything else.

leader.title: Boss
leader.name: Gazlowe
leader.line: Neutral ain't a principle, friend. It's a business model, and it's the only one that keeps a port open when everyone on both sides wants it.

lore: The Cartel is not a nation, an army or a cause. It is a company with harbours, and the harbours are the only places on this coast where a Horde ship and an Alliance ship tie up on the same pier and nobody draws anything.

That neutrality is enforced, and the enforcement is the actual product. Bring a war into Ratchet and the Cartel will not take a side; it will remove you, bill your faction for the inconvenience, and reopen by the evening tide.

Gazlowe runs the port, and runs it better than the margins justify. He has turned down three offers to move the operation somewhere richer, which no goblin will explain and several have tried to buy him out over.

Standing with the Cartel is simple and entirely transactional: they like people who are good for trade and hard on the things that interrupt it. Pirates off the coast and bandits on the Barrens road cost them money, and they pay well to have that stopped. Nobody at Ratchet will pretend this is friendship, and that honesty is most of why people deal with them.

kill_rep._comment: Whatever interrupts trade: pirates on the water, bandits on the Barrens road. The Cartel pays per head and does not care about your politics.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. The system supports them; the content is not written.

thunder_bluff.name: Thunder Bluff
thunder_bluff.description: A nation that still answers to the name of a city that is no longer standing. The tauren lost Mulgore in the Integration and have been guests in other people's towns since.
thunder_bluff.home_name: Camp Taurajo, the Southern Barrens - in exile

leader.title: Elder
leader.name: Longtread
leader.line: I am not the High Chieftain. I am the one standing where he would be standing, and I will go on doing it until somebody tells me to stop or he comes back and tells me himself.

thunder_bluff._leader_note: Longtread speaks for the tauren but holds no title, because Cairne Bloodhoof is MISSING rather than confirmed dead. Nobody has taken the office. Taking it would be a ruling on where he is.
lore: Thunder Bluff stood on four rock spires above Mulgore and had never been taken. When the Integration rewrote the world three years ago it did not take the city either. It took the ground the city was standing on.

What is left of Mulgore is not a ruin, which the tauren could have worked with. It is a nightmare land - the plain went wrong in a way nobody has a vocabulary for, and the things walking it now kill experienced war parties without slowing down. The tauren have mounted four attempts to reach the spires. They do not discuss the fourth.

So they are guests. Forty at Camp Taurajo, a warband through the southern Barrens, and the rest scattered into other people's capitals - a leatherworker in Orgrimmar, a quartermaster at Splintertree, shamans on the Barrens oases, and more turning up in places nobody expected as word spreads that there is somewhere to turn up to. Every nation that took them in did so immediately and without conditions, and the tauren have been scrupulously, exhaustingly grateful ever since, which costs them more than anyone watching understands.

They have not renamed themselves and they have not filled the chieftain's office. Cairne Bloodhoof walked out of a council three years ago and did not come back, and nothing since has established whether he died on the plain or is still somewhere on it. Elder Longtread speaks for the tauren, carefully, in the first person plural, and has refused every suggestion that he take the title. Taking it would be a ruling on where Cairne is, and the tauren are not prepared to make one.

Standing with them is not earned by sympathy, which they have had enough of. It is earned by helping them hold the ground they still have - and by being the sort of person who might, eventually, be worth taking back onto the plain.

kill_rep._comment: What presses on the ground they have left: quilboar raiding the camps, and the Bael'dun dwarves digging a plain that is not theirs while the tauren watch a worse one from a distance.

rewards._comment: No gates authored yet. When Mulgore is built as the level 60 zone, this is where its access and its rewards belong.
